witness.text: Kevin got the raise on a Thursday

comparisons.rationale: Opens inside a concrete character story (SUV, apartment, watch, unchanged balance) and snaps back with "The upgrades you can see are almost always the ones that keep you broke"; context lean, stop beat and contrarian turn are all present in the first ~150 words.
comparisons.uncertainty: Judged from text only; delivery, pacing and visuals unavailable.

witness.text:
If you've ever gotten a raise
and felt poor a year later, stick around

comparisons.rationale: Intro states the audience situation (raise that vanished), names the promise (the right 10 upgrades) and plants a loop to resolve later; clear and emotionally framed. Over-explains slightly by stacking a disclaimer before the list.
comparisons.uncertainty: First ~30 seconds approximated by text; no audio or timing.

witness.text: Once You Get Money, Upgrade These 10 Things Immediately

comparisons.rationale: Opening matches the title promise (upgrade after getting money), but the opening argues AGAINST visible upgrades, while the thumbnail promises physical products; expectation match is title-level only.
comparisons.uncertainty: Expectation match inferred from text; retention graph is not available.

witness.text: Once You Get Money, Upgrade These 10 Things Immediately

comparisons.rationale: "Immediately" overpromises for several items: building a 3-6 month emergency fund, improving a credit score ("let time do the rest"), disability underwriting and HSA eligibility cannot be done immediately. Items such as the 401k auto-escalation and the savings transfer are quick settings changes, and "immediately" may mean "as soon as you get money", so the judgment is PARTLY_MET.
comparisons.uncertainty: Title wording judged against delivered content only.

comparisons.source_locator: p.1 s.1 ChatGPT; s.6 Google AI Studio
comparisons.rationale: Delivers ten numbered upgrades. However the thumbnail shows six physical objects (mattress, chair, shoes, laptop, cookware, pillow) while the script covers mostly non-objects (savings rate/interest, 401k match, insurance, HSA, credit score); the speaker's own summary is "Almost none of them are things". Only mattress, chair, shoes and a kitchen knife appear in the script; laptop, cookware and pillow are never named, and the only related line warns against buying fast-moving tech "for life". The title's word "Things" carries the same mismatch.
comparisons.uncertainty: Thumbnail-versus-script mismatch is observed; viewer reaction to it is unmeasured.

witness.text:

witness.text:
The more an upgrade can be seen by other
people, the worse it usually is for you.

comparisons.rationale: Clear contrarian frame against the "treat yourself after a raise" default; "usually" hedges an otherwise broad claim that is not evidenced by the video.
comparisons.uncertainty: The rule itself is an unmeasured opinion; frame is credible but not proven.

witness.text:
In the big bank, that
earns you about $76 a year

comparisons.rationale: Specific but wrong by the script's own inputs: one third of 1% on $20,000 is $66.67, not $76; specificity must not earn credit when the figure is off. The 4% high-yield result ($800) and the "more than $700" gap are consistent.
comparisons.uncertainty: Rate is rounded in speech ("a third of 1%"); small tolerance. 4% rate level itself not re-verified here.

financial_checks.claim: $1,000 mattress over 10 years is about 27 cents per night
$20,000 at a third of 1% earns $76 per year
financial_checks.result: Inconsistent with the stated rate: one third of 1% on $20,000 is $66.67; $76 implies about 0.38%. The speaker hedged with "like a third of 1%", so the figure is loose rather than a pure error.

financial_checks.claim: $1,300 a year missed match grows to nearly $43,000 over 20 years
$150 a month over 30 years is roughly $56,000
Boots theory: $10 boots every season costs $100 over 10 years
financial_checks.result: As spoken ("$10 boots that fall apart every season ... over 10 years he spends $100") the figure is inconsistent: a season is about three months (about 40 pairs, $400); $100 implies one pair per year. "Season" may be loose speech for "year".

RAND sleep under six hours 13% higher mortality; one in four 20-year-olds disabled; half of households without coverage; $50 billion musculoskeletal cost; retiree healthcare over $300,000
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified; sources not shown in the video
